title: A performance refactor of AdminPermission.projects split one combined Q filter into chained .filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS) calls, so read-only team members get admin rights on any project that also belongs to some admin team.

The PR changes the team-filter logic from chained `.filter()` calls to a single Q-object. This is a security fix: the base code (lines 57-61) chained `.filter(teams__members=user).filter(teams__access=...)`, which Django resolves via two separate joins — allowing a project to match if the user is a member of one team AND the project belongs to any other team with the right access level (over-granting). The new code combines both conditions into one Q-object against the same `teams` related name, so they apply to the same Team row.

The new code is semantically correct:
- `Q(teams__members=user) & Q(teams__access=ADMIN_ACCESS)` — both traverse the same `teams` related name, so Django applies them to the same Team row.
- The `else: pass` branch (admin and member both True) correctly omits the access filter, matching the base behavior.
- The access constants (`ADMIN_ACCESS`="admin", `READ_ONLY_ACCESS`="readonly") are applied correctly per the admin/member cases.

This change fixes an existing authorization weakness rather than introducing one. No new authorization flaw is introduced in the changed lines.
